extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners subject to USPTO disciplinary proceedings; attorneys and counsel involved in OED matters; OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Adjudication of whether a registered patent practitioner complied with the terms of a USPTO Final Order and whether the stay of suspension should be vacated. Includes procedural requirements for notice, show-cause, proof of compliance, and consequences for violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with terms of the Final Order (stay condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Respondent's suspension will be stayed, and he will be permitted to continue to practice, so long as he complies with the terms of this Final Order." (Final Order, ¶ 99b) Failure to comply causes the stay to be vacated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per Final Order ¶99c: "In the event Respondent fails to comply with any of the terms of this Final Order, the stay of suspension will be immediately vacated and Respondent shall serve a three-year suspension... prior to being eligible for reinstatement." The decision enforces objective compliance with the terms—noncompliance triggers the stated automatic consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of initial and scheduled payments to designated clients (paragraph 99f)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order required Respondent to provide a $500 or $1,000 initial payment to each client on the designated list by June 15, 2008, and to make quarterly payments thereafter according to the payment schedule reflected in the Final Order (¶99f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments had to be made (or at least mailed so clients would receive them) by the specified date. The OED found that mailing on June 27, 2008 (and clients receiving checks on July 1), was untimely. The respondent's explanation that June 15 fell on a Sunday and that checks were prepared but mailed later was rejected; late mailing/receipt is noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to designated clients and content requirements (paragraph 99h/99g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of the Final Order, Respondent was required to notify in writing all clients on the designated list of his partial refund to them and the schedule for repayment, and to include specific paragraphs as set forth in the Final Order (¶99h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications must include the specified language and be provided within the time required. The OED scrutinized unsigned letters and late notices; the Final Order also required notification of bars of which respondent is a member and prompt confirmation to the OED (¶99g). Failure to follow content/timing requirements is noncompliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of mailing/ability to substantiate compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent should be able to substantiate mailing and delivery (e.g., certified mail numbers and postage dates) for required communications and payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED attempted to verify certified mail numbers with USPS and noted inconsistencies (postage dates after the due date). Providing copies of letters with certified mail numbers while failing to disclose that they had not actually been mailed undermines the respondent's compliance showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of candor and timely communication with the OED
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must accurately and promptly inform the OED of the status of required actions; withholding that letters had not been mailed or otherwise failing to disclose material facts is improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED noted that although respondent provided copies of letters dated June 16 on June 23, he failed to inform the OED that the letters had not been mailed as of June 23. Such failures to disclose relevant facts weigh against maintaining a stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due diligence — human error is not a per se excuse
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim that noncompliance resulted from inadvertent human error does not excuse violating provisions that are central to the Final Order; the respondent must exercise due diligence to ensure required actions are completed timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision found respondent 'did not intentionally fail' but nonetheless 'knowingly did not act on or before June 15' and 'at best failed to exercise due diligence.' Courts/OED treat failure to exercise due diligence as insufficient to avoid the consequences of noncompliance with core obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement: issuance of Order To Show Cause and response period
rubrics_metrics.description: Before vacating a stayed suspension, USPTO must provide an Order To Show Cause explaining why the stay should be vacated and give the respondent ten calendar days to file a reply (as provided in the Final Order ¶99d and implemented by the OED Director).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director issued an Order To Show Cause (July 9, 2008) giving ten days to respond; earlier Orders may be withdrawn if procedural defects exist. After the response period, the Director may exercise discretion to vacate the stay consistent with the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement of prescribed disciplinary consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order prescribes that vacatur of the stay results in immediate service of the three-year suspension starting when the stay is vacated, before eligibility for reinstatement (¶99c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision applied this remedy: the stay was vacated and a three-year suspension ordered under 37 C.F.R. § 10.158. The Final Order's specified sanction is binding when its triggering conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of judicial review/appeal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may seek judicial review in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia under 35 U.S.C. § 32 and Local Rule 213 within thirty (30) days of entry of the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notifies the respondent of the avenue and timeline for pursuing review in federal court; procedural timeliness for appeal is strict.
